topic: Memory Hierarchy and Caching Strategies: Speeds Costs
explanation: Modern computer systems employ a memory hierarchy to balance cost and performance.  This hierarchy consists of multiple levels of memory with varying speeds and costs.  Faster, smaller, and more expensive memory (like caches) sits closer to the CPU, while slower, larger, and cheaper memory (like main memory and disk) sits further away.  Caching strategies exploit the principle of locality (temporal and spatial) to minimize the time it takes to access data. Data frequently accessed is stored in faster memory levels, reducing average access time.
